step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes an automated AWS account vending machine. The process begins with an internal user interacting with a web portal, which sends a request via API Gateway. This triggers an AWS Step Functions workflow (named 'AVM' for Account Vending Machine). This Step Functions instance interacts with DynamoDB to store and retrieve account state, ensuring idempotency. The AVM then orchestrates the creation of the AWS account via AWS Control Tower. After the account is created, the AVM triggers another AWS Step Functions workflow (named 'Blueprint') responsible for applying various configurations (IAM, security, networking) to the newly provisioned AWS Account. Finally, an email notification is sent to the user via SES, confirming account readiness.

graph.name: Vitesco Technologies Cloud Foundation Account Vending Machine
graph.notes: This architecture depicts Vitesco Technologies' Cloud Foundation, an end-to-end automated cloud landing zone. It enables internal users to quickly create AWS accounts that are configured according to company standards and AWS best practices. The diagram focuses on the initial account provisioning and blueprint deployment process.

nodes.name: Vitesco Technologies User
nodes.notes: An internal user at Vitesco Technologies requesting a new AWS account via a self-developed web portal.

nodes.name: Self-developed Web Portal API
nodes.notes: Receives the account creation requests initiated by users through their internal web portal.

nodes.name: Account Vending Machine (AVM)
nodes.notes: Orchestrates the entire account creation process, managing steps from request initiation to blueprint deployment. Referred to as the 'account vending machine' in the transcript.

nodes.name: Account State Database
nodes.notes: Stores all information describing the target state of the account, including user input and dynamically generated data like VPC CIDA ranges and account IDs. Ensures idempotency of the process.

nodes.name: Control Tower Account Creation
nodes.notes: Responsible for creating the actual AWS accounts. This is currently done via a custom Service Catalog item because Control Tower does not provide an API for this functionality.

nodes.name: New AWS Account
nodes.notes: The target AWS account provisioned for the Vitesco Technologies user, configured with company blueprints.

nodes.name: Blueprint Deployment
nodes.notes: Deploys various configurations, or 'blueprints', into the newly created AWS account. These blueprints include IAM, security services (e.g., SecurityHub, GuardDuty, AWS Config), and network configurations (e.g., VPC, subnets, Route53, Transit Gateway attachment).

nodes.name: Email Notification Service
nodes.notes: Sends an email notification to the user once the account is fully deployed and configured, providing access instructions and outlining account owner responsibilities.

edges.notes: User submits a request for a new AWS account via a self-developed web portal, which sends the request to API Gateway.
API Gateway forwards the account request to the Account Vending Machine (AVM) Step Functions workflow.
The AVM Step Functions writes the desired target state and metadata of the account to DynamoDB.
The AVM Step Functions reads from DynamoDB to ensure idempotency and retrieve current account state during the process.
The AVM Step Functions triggers AWS Control Tower (via a custom Service Catalog item) to create the new AWS account.
AWS Control Tower provisions the new AWS account.
After account creation, the AVM Step Functions triggers the Blueprint Deployment Step Functions to apply necessary configurations.
The Blueprint Deployment Step Functions applies various configurations (IAM, security, network blueprints) to the newly provisioned AWS Account.
Once all blueprints are deployed, the Blueprint Deployment Step Functions sends a notification via SES.
The user receives an email notification confirming the new AWS account is ready, along with access details and responsibilities.
